Hey, my realtor just mentioned something about needing to set up an escrow account for my house purchase here in Toronto. I've never dealt with this before, can you explain what escrow actually is and why it's used during the closing process?

Sure thing—think of an escrow as the “neutral‑party vault” that holds the money (and sometimes documents) while the house deal goes from offer to closing. In Toronto (and the rest of Ontario), the buyer’s lawyer or a licensed escrow‑agent receives the deposit, the mortgage funds and any other required amounts, keeps them safe, and then releases them to the seller (or the seller’s lawyer) only when all the conditions in the purchase agreement have been satisfied—title search cleared, inspections done, financing approved, etc. This protects both sides: the buyer isn’t forced to hand over cash before the seller has done his part, and the seller knows the money is already there and won’t disappear at the last minute.

That makes sense. So basically it's just a middleman to make sure nobody gets ripped off? Is there anything specific I need to watch out for when I'm transferring the money into that account so things don't go wrong?

Exactly—think of escrow as the “middle‑man guard post” where the money sits safely until every condition in the purchase agreement is met, so neither the buyer nor the seller gets short‑changed. When you wire the funds, double‑check the **bank‑account details** (routing number, institution name, and account number) that your lawyer or escrow agent provides—mistyping a digit is the most common way a payment can end up in a stranger’s pocket, and it’s tough to retrieve. Escrow agents must keep the funds in a **segregated, interest‑bearing trust account** that is separate from their own operating money, and they are legally prohibited from using the cash for any purpose other than the transaction at hand. They also have to follow strict **audit and reporting rules**—the account is regularly reconciled, and any disbursement can only occur after all contractual conditions are documented as satisfied.
